findings.title: Wire the new timeout into the shutdown drain
findings.problem: A supported value such as shutdown_drain_timeout=120.5 is accepted but ignored. triggarr/search/scheduler.py:70–81 still derives its timeout solely from the environment or a hard-coded 60 seconds, and line 634 uses that constant. With no environment override, shutdown therefore forces resource closure after 60 seconds despite the configured longer drain, potentially interrupting an in-flight search. No runtime caller reads the new field.
findings.why_it_matters: A supported value such as shutdown_drain_timeout=120.5 is accepted but ignored. triggarr/search/scheduler.py:70–81 still derives its timeout solely from the environment or a hard-coded 60 seconds, and line 634 uses that constant. With no environment override, shutdown therefore forces resource closure after 60 seconds despite the configured longer drain, potentially interrupting an in-flight search. No runtime caller reads the new field.
findings.fix_hint: Use settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout as the shutdown timeout default, apply the explicit environment override, and add an integration test proving a nondefault config value reaches the drain.

members.title: Comment describes env-override and form-clamp behavior that is not implemented
members.problem: Nothing in triggarr/ reads GeneralConfig.shutdown_drain_timeout. The scheduler still uses the import-time constant `_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` (scheduler.py:81, used at 611-656), and no 3600.0 form clamp exists in web/routes.py. The comment says 'env overrides at shutdown' and 'form clamp (3600.0) is the UI ceiling' as if both already work. This looks like a TDD step partway through phase 75 (commit 9bfd4a6 adds the failing test first). pending: confirm later phase-75 plans wire the scheduler and form before release.
